To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The competition between rice and a diverse weed flora for light and nitrogen is simulated with an age-structured population model.

(1) A model that simulates the growth and yield of rice and weeds in response to nitrogen and light competition is presented; (2) The model predictions agree reasonably well with field observations of the growth and development of weeds and rice; (3) The simulation model can be used to examine the effects of weed competition on rice yield and to determine the optimal timing of weed control.

(i) weed control is more effective when weeds are removed at an early stage, and (ii) weed control is most effective when weeds are controlled before the rice plants are 30 cm tall, and least effective when weeds are not removed until the rice plants are taller than 50 cm.
